Variants.Content: The Sorrows lie along the middle reaches of the Rhoyne around the ruins of the ancient city of Chroyane. Once a Rhoynish water city destroyed in the wars against Valyria, today river mists, broken bridges, Stone Men, and rumors of greyscale make ships fearful of drawing near; this place belongs to no stable city-state, resembling instead a historical wound encircled by river water.
Entry Sorrowland Local families also relied on dyes, glass, weaving, orchards, and ever-rerouted trade travel; any time a road, well, or dock failed, the price fell first to them.

Entry Sorrowland They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of Myr and disputed lands; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, and true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Sorrowland If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.

Stone and timber may rot, yet the Sorrows still endure through artisans who tend stone walls, wooden beams, iron gates, crypts, and the seams left by generations of repairs, and through priests who preserve the temples of the gods, guild traditions, and old walls left by the wars of the Free Cities. A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Sorrowland They care about dyes, glass, weaving, orchards, and the ever-changing trade routes. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
